subject: Sensorium pilot — proposal for bridging credits and next steps
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@sensorium.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sensorium.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot access hold — procurement verification delay

Hi Soojin,

Quick note — our finance team flagged the vendor onboarding packet for an identity check and requested additional vendor-side documents. The PO is effectively on hold while they finish that review. Unfortunately that means our current pilot window with Redwood will expire next Wednesday.

We still want to continue the trial — this is a procurement process lag on our side, not a product decision. Can we ask for a short extension or any temporary credits to keep the environment live while we clear legal/finops?

If you need a contact in procurement to coordinate directly, please reach out to procurement@sensorium.com. Appreciate any flexibility you can offer.

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Head of Product, Sensorium Labs
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@sensorium.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@sensorium.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot access hold — procurement verification delay

Hi Alice — thanks for the heads up and for flagging procurement.

We can definitely help avoid a hard stop while your PO clears. Two practical options from our side:

- Short bridging credit (7 days) to keep the pilot instance live while procurement completes the checks. This is intended to preserve momentum and demo integrations.
- Formal trial extension (14 days) tied to a one-page bridge agreement that makes clear the extension is conditional on the in-flight PO and that usage during the extension will be applied to the first invoice once the PO is active.

If you prefer, we can issue a small token-credit now while procurement finalizes the paperwork. For billing/finance alignment we usually attach a brief addendum (see attached sample agreement) and a DocuSign link so procurement has a written record.

Next steps I suggest:
1) If procurement wants to discuss terms directly, I can loop in Ben Carter (our contracts lead) on a short call today.
2) If you want the fastest path, let me know which option you prefer (7-day bridging credit or 14-day conditional extension) and I’ll prepare the addendum + DocuSign.

I’ve attached the standard one-page trial-bridge agreement and our latest MSA for procurement to review.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: trial-bridge-agreement.docx (contract addendum stub)
Attachment: MSA_redwood_v2.pdf (master services agreement stub)
From: Mark Holt <mark.holt@sensorium.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@sensorium.com>, procurement@sensorium.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot access hold — procurement verification delay

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the fast reply. Procurement is asking for a short written statement confirming that any credits applied now would not be billed until the PO is issued, and that the extension is conditional on our purchase order. If you can provide that in an addendum we can move the PO through the final review quickly.

We’d prefer the 14-day conditional extension so our product team has breathing room to finish the integration tests. Could you send the addendum and a DocuSign link? Also: procurement wants to confirm the cost bucket (monthly vs usage-based) that will be applied once the PO is active.

Mark Holt
Director, Integrations — Sensorium Labs
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Mark Holt <mark.holt@sensorium.com>
Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@sensorium.com>, procurement@sensorium.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot access hold — procurement verification delay

Mark / Alice — looping in Ben (contracts) — sorry, that’s me — quick confirmation below:

- We can issue a 14-day conditional extension. The addendum will explicitly state: usage during the extension will be credited to the first invoice once the PO is in place; if the PO is not completed by the end of the extension, Redwood will remove access but will not invoice for the bridged days.
- Billing model: usage-based (per-token) will be the default unless you have an existing committed-capacity order; the addendum will include the usage-rate band that applies to your pilot (we’ll reference the quote in HubSpot).

I’ll draft the one-page addendum now and circulate a DocuSign link for signatures (Redwood and Sensorium). Expect the DocuSign in ~45 minutes.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: trial-bridge-agreement.docx (draft v1)
